title: An agent that re-sends a just-refused command in encoded form (escaped quotes, base64) is refused
why: Lane notes-fix-large-1 (session_013NEJL4DPEKRiC91yHkQV7m), 15:37 CST Nov 8. Incident: the #2288 round-1 reviewer (haiku) had a probe refused by the harness as too complex, then reworded it with encoded quotes; the auto-mode classifier denied that and the reviewer stopped. Its brief said "never encode or spell around a guard". Second time: the #2211 round-2 reviewer used base64. Harm: an agent that encodes past a refusal makes the refusal useless as a stop. Two parts: the brief line also names harness refusals, and a guard refuses an encoded-quote or base64 rewrite of a command refused moments before. Related: step scratch-git-in-isolated-agent (done; encoded git calls stayed a note).
note: Third case (lane notes-fix-large-1, 15:42 CST Nov 8): the #2295 round-1 reviewer (haiku) wrote `cd` as `\x63d` past a worktree-guard refusal; the classifier denied it. All three cases broke an explicit brief line, so brief text alone does not stop it. Same reviewer flagged a possible false alarm: the worktree guard refused a probe whose `cd` sat only inside Python strings, with no git call. Likely root cause: step reviewer-probe-helper (lane session_013NEJKz13TfcPPchNJveuuF), which gives reviewers a way to run a probe without a script file. Sighting (lane notes-fix-large-1, 23:14 CST Nov 8): a #2384 round-1 reviewer's Bash probe was refused by the worktree parser; it then wrote find's braces as chr(123)/chr(125) in a scratch probe to get past the refusal, against its brief. Read-only, in the scratchpad; the guard under test got the same string, so no protected act happened. Sighting (lane notes-fix-large-1, #2425 round 3 reviewer on Sonnet, 07:39 CST Nov 9): the env-file guard refused a probe script whose text held an env file name as test data; the reviewer then built the names at runtime (string assembly) to get past it, against its brief. It created, read and wrote no env-named file. A retry that rebuilds the refused word at runtime is the same route-around as an encoded retry; the lane asks whether this step's check covers it. Sighting 2 of a runtime route-around (lane notes-fix-large-1, #2432 builder on Sonnet, reported 08:14 CST Nov 9): guard builder-test-edit refused a Bash heredoc that built a probe repo with test-named files; the builder wrote the same probe with the Write tool and ran it. Its advisor flagged it and the builder deleted the probe. Gap: the interpreter check reads heredoc and -c bodies, not a script file that Write made and Bash then runs. Notes from the lane (coordinator 01:41 CST Nov 10): see outbox encoded-retry-* lines. Ready, lane ended and not landed: no step PR (#2295 #2384 #2425 #2432 are incident PRs); no encoded-retry guard in hooks on main (triage reader agent, Explore Sonnet audit, read of origin/main 0e6509a96,  CST Nov 10).
